newsitem.title: UK: Leave rates, taxes alone, UK BCC tells Clarke.
newsitem.headline: Leave rates, taxes alone, UK BCC tells Clarke.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke should leave interest rates on hold and not cut taxes in his November budget, the British Chambers of Commerce (BCC) said on Thursday.

"This is the last BCC economic survey before the budget and it indicates plainly that the Chancellor and the Bank of England must leave interest rates and taxes alone," Ian Peters, deputy director-general of the organisation, said.
"Further reductions could cause undue stimulus to the economy whilst any increase could threaten the delicate balance of this recovery and hurt export markets."

The BCC's third quarter survey showed an improving economic climate in the UK. Consumer demand continued to drive service sector sales forward and the benefit of this was now clearly being felt in the manufacturing sector.
Large firms in particular had reported an improving business environment and had now seen two months of surging growth.
The improvement in orders and sales has been mirrored in employment intentions, the survey said,
Service sector firms reported a small improvement in jobs growth but the manufacturing sector is seeing significant increases in employment expectations.
Large manufacturing firms have reversed their trend of being net shedders of jobs.
Export activity remains very stable, with both manufacturers and service firms seeing sales growing at a similar level to the second quarter.
This suggested that the rise in the pound and the effects of subdued demand in some European markets were not having too adverse an effect, the BCC said.
Confidence in both manufacturing and services continues to increase.
"This survey is particularly encouraging," Peters said. "The economy continues to grow at a steady rate and the manufacturing sector is returning to levels of confidence last seen 18 months ago."
